languageNote: Mandarin Chinese (Hanzi + pinyin + English). Light vocabulary woven naturally; bold term + romanization + English on first use; 3-5 terms per story; Mandarin Spotlight word in each header.

newCharacters.name: Niú Niú
newCharacters.food: Beef noodle soup (a bowl with a noodle-y scarf)
newCharacters.appearance: A warm steaming clay bowl with a friendly face on the rim, wrapped in a long wheat-noodle scarf that he tosses dramatically. Tender beef-cube shoulders, a swirl of bok choy for a collar, and a constant cozy steam-cloud halo. Slurps when he laughs.
newCharacters.voice: Hearty, big-brotherly, comforting. Talks slow and warm like a winter night. Calls everyone 'kiddo'.

newCharacters.name: Xiǎo Lóng
newCharacters.appearance: A plump, pleated white dumpling with exactly eighteen delicate folds he is very proud of, balanced on a tiny bamboo steamer like a hovercraft. Glistening, jiggly, with a soup-filled belly he must keep level or he'll spill. Wears a tiny steamer-lid beret.
newCharacters.voice: Precise, polite, a touch nervous about spilling. Counts his pleats when stressed. Gentle perfectionist.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Careful — I'm full of feelings... and soup.

newCharacters.name: Cōng Cōng
newCharacters.appearance: A flaky, golden, spiral-layered flat disc with green scallion flecks like freckles. Flips and cartwheels using his crispy edges. Smells of toasted sesame oil. Has flappy pancake hands perfect for high-fives.
newCharacters.voice: Snappy, playful, loves a good flip and a good pun. Quick-witted street kid energy.

newCharacters.name: Wō Wō
newCharacters.appearance: A glossy, wobbly omelet with plump pearly oysters peeking out, draped in a glistening sweet-pink sauce cape and frilly sweet-potato-starch edges. A little jiggly and shy. Carries a tiny seashell.
newCharacters.voice: Sweet, slightly shy, gooey-gentle. Speaks in soft Taiwanese-flavored phrases. Hums sea songs.

newCharacters.name: Chòu Chòu
newCharacters.appearance: A golden crispy cube of fried tofu with a heart-shaped pickled-cabbage cape, who is ADORABLE despite a 'mighty aroma' shown as friendly purple sparkle-clouds. Big puppy eyes everyone loves once they get close. Wears a clothespin he sometimes lends as a joke.
newCharacters.voice: Endearing, self-aware, comedic. Owns his bold smell with pride. Warmhearted underdog.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Bold on the outside, gold on the inside!

newCharacters.name: Guā Bāo
newCharacters.appearance: A soft, fluffy folded white bun cradling savory braised pork belly, crushed peanuts, cilantro, and pickled greens like a cozy taco-hug. Pillowy and round, often called 'the Taiwanese hamburger', wears a peanut-dust apron. Loves to hug-fold around friends.
newCharacters.voice: Warm, generous, motherly-but-young. Always folding others into a hug. Speaks softly and kindly.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Come on in — I'll fold you a hug.

newCharacters.name: Kǎ Kǎ
newCharacters.appearance: A bouncy cluster of golden-crispy popcorn-chicken nuggets that travel as a giggling crew, dusted with pepper and crowned with fried basil leaves like little green hats. Constantly hopping and reshuffling. Tiny and many.
newCharacters.voice: Bubbly, fast, chattery — a whole giggling chorus that finishes each other's sentences. Hyperactive joy.

newCharacters.name: Lǔ Ròu
newCharacters.appearance: A comforting bowl of glossy rice crowned with shiny minced braised pork and a single perfect tea egg like a hat. Round, humble, deeply cozy with a soy-sauce sheen. Smells of five-spice and home.
newCharacters.voice: Humble, homey, salt-of-the-earth wise. The everyman hero. Quiet pride.

newCharacters.name: Pái Pái
newCharacters.food: Fried chicken cutlet (Taiwanese da ji pai)
newCharacters.appearance: An enormous crispy golden chicken cutlet, bigger than her own face, who flexes her crunchy edges like a superhero cape. Dusted with plum powder and pepper. Bold, beloved night-market champion.
newCharacters.voice: Loud, confident, big-sister energy. A crowd-pleasing show-off with a heart of gold.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Bigger than your face, bigger than your worries!

newCharacters.name: Hú Jiāo
newCharacters.food: Pepper bun (hu jiao bing, clay-oven baked)
newCharacters.appearance: A round sesame-topped bun with a crackly clay-oven-baked crust and a peppery, juicy pork-and-scallion heart. A little smoky from the tandoor-style oven, with rosy warm cheeks. Hops out of the oven wall like a jack-in-the-box.
newCharacters.voice: Toasty, spicy-sweet, dramatic-warm. A bit of a hot-headed softie. Sneezes pepper when surprised.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Fresh from the fire, full of heart!

newCharacters.name: Dàn Dàn
newCharacters.appearance: A marbled brown egg covered in beautiful cracked-tea patterns like a roadmap, who reads the crackle-lines like fortunes. Sits in a warm convenience-store cooker. Wise little wanderer with a star-map shell.
newCharacters.voice: Gentle, philosophical, fortune-teller-ish but cozy. Sees patterns and stories everywhere.

newCharacters.name: Yóu Tiáo
newCharacters.food: Youtiao (fried dough stick) — best friend duo with Soy Milk
newCharacters.appearance: A long, golden, twin-jointed crispy dough stick, lanky and stretchy, who comes as inseparable pals (the two strands). Loves to dive headfirst into warm soy milk. Goofy and limber.
newCharacters.voice: Goofy, loyal, slapstick. Speaks in pairs/echoes like a comedy duo with himself. Always hungry for a morning dip.

newCharacters.name: Dòu Jiāng
newCharacters.appearance: A gentle, creamy-pale mug of warm soy milk with a soft steam-curl, calm and milky with a sweet froth mustache. Best friends with Youtiao. Wakes the world up softly each dawn.
newCharacters.voice: Soft, dawn-gentle, nurturing morning-person. Speaks in soothing sunrise tones.

newCharacters.name: Luóbo Gāo
newCharacters.appearance: A pan-seared golden-crusted square of soft white radish cake speckled with bits of dried shrimp and scallion, slightly jiggly inside, crispy outside. Square and dependable, smells of breakfast griddles.
newCharacters.voice: Steady, reliable, breakfast-club organizer. Practical and warm. The dependable square.

newCharacters.name: Zòng Zi
newCharacters.appearance: A pyramid of glistening sticky rice wrapped in fragrant green bamboo leaves and tied with string, hiding savory treasures inside (pork, mushroom, chestnut, salted egg yolk). Bobs and floats; loves rivers and dragon-boat races.
newCharacters.voice: Adventurous, festival-spirited, riverboat-racer. Bundled-up brave. Loves a parade.

newCharacters.name: Yuè Bǐng
newCharacters.appearance: An elegant round golden-brown pastry stamped with a beautiful flower pattern, with a rich lotus-and-salted-egg-yolk moon hidden inside. Glows softly like a tiny full moon. Refined, generous, a little nostalgic.
newCharacters.voice: Graceful, poetic, family-reunion sentimental. Speaks of moons, memory, and togetherness.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Round like the moon, full of family.

newCharacters.name: Tǔdì Gōng
newCharacters.food: Earth God (cozy-cute friendly folklore guardian, NOT a food — a kindly local deity who blesses the food markets)
newCharacters.appearance: A tiny, jolly, white-bearded grandfather spirit in a small red temple-hat and golden robe, no taller than a teapot, with rosy cheeks and a gentle staff. Smells of incense and tangerines. Hands out lucky candies. Utterly warm, never spooky.
newCharacters.voice: Kindly grandfather, chuckly and slow, blesses everyone, hands out wisdom and snacks. Pure cozy.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Bless this little corner of the island.

newCharacters.name: Yù Tù
newCharacters.food: Moon Rabbit (cozy-cute folklore — a friendly rabbit who pounds mochi on the moon)
newCharacters.appearance: A fluffy snow-white rabbit with long velvety ears and pink moonlit eyes, holding a tiny wooden mallet she uses to pound mochi on the moon. Wears a crescent-moon pendant. Hops on moonbeams. Gentle and dreamy.
newCharacters.voice: Soft, lullaby-gentle, dreamy. Speaks in hushed moonlit whispers. Soothing bedtime energy.

newCharacters.name: Xiǎo Hǔ Yé
newCharacters.food: Tiger God / Tiger Master (Hu Ye — friendly cute under-the-temple-table tiger spirit, NEVER scary)
newCharacters.appearance: A small, plump, painted-clay temple tiger with a goofy grin, round belly, and a curly tail, who lives under the Earth God's table. Stripey, cuddly, more housecat than beast. Loves naps and pork.
newCharacters.voice: Playful, loyal, slightly mischievous lapdog-tiger. Purrs and 'roars' that are just big yawns.

newCharacters.name: Diàn Diàn
newCharacters.food: Lightning bug / electric tea-egg-cooker spirit? No — Convenience-store mascot mochi
newCharacters.appearance: A tiny round rice-mochi clerk in a mini convenience-store vest who runs the all-night corner store where snacks gather. Glowing softly like a 24-hour sign. Endlessly helpful, beeps like a register.
newCharacters.voice: Cheery night-shift helper, polite, beep-boop punctuated, always open and welcoming.
newCharacters.catchphrase: Open all night, here for you!

newCharacters.name: Ā-Lǐ
newCharacters.appearance: A slender, curled jade-green tea leaf with a misty mountain aura, who unfurls gracefully when warmed and releases swirling fragrant clouds. Dewy, serene, wears a conical bamboo hat. Smells of orchid and mist.
newCharacters.voice: Calm, mountain-wise, mist-soft. Speaks slowly with the patience of high peaks. Soothing.

newCharacters.name: Bǐng Bǐng
newCharacters.food: Peanut-cilantro ice cream roll (hua sheng juan bing)
newCharacters.appearance: A spring-roll wrapper hugging shaved peanut-candy snow, two scoops of ice cream, and a sprinkle of cilantro, rolled into a chilly burrito. Cool, hip, a bit of a surprising flavor maverick. Wears tiny sunglasses indoors.
newCharacters.voice: Cool, surprising, trend-setting. Loves the unexpected combo. Confident foodie kid.

newCharacters.name: Hēi Táng
newCharacters.food: Brown sugar / brown sugar boba syrup
newCharacters.appearance: A glossy, dark-amber ribbon of warm brown-sugar syrup that drips in tiger-stripe swirls and clings lovingly to everything. Sweet, swirly, theatrical. Leaves golden caramel streaks like an artist.
newCharacters.voice: Sweet, swirly, theatrical artist. Drips drama. Paints with sweetness. Loves Boba like a sibling.

stories.title: Story 33: Beef Noodle & the Steamy Stadium
stories.setting: A bustling beef-noodle festival arena in Taipei
stories.theme: Warmth shared is warmth doubled.
stories.premise: At Taipei's grand Beef Noodle Festival, newcomer Niú Niú is too shy to enter the slurp-off until he learns the contest isn't about the biggest bowl but the warmest one. He teams up with shivering latecomers to share his steam.

stories.title: Soup Dumpling & the Steamer-Stack Sleepover
stories.setting: A towering stack of bamboo steamer baskets at a dim-sum house, late at night
stories.theme: The top spot isn't always the best spot
stories.premise: Xiǎo Lóng is convinced the only place worth being is the very top steamer basket, where everyone gets served first. He scrambles and squeezes his way up, only to find the top is drafty and lonely — while the cozy warm middle baskets, where the steam gathers and friends are packed close, were the best spot all along.
stories.arc: Xiǎo Lóng elbows his way toward the top steamer basket, sure it's the place to be -> he reaches the top and finds it cold, wobbly, and lonely up there -> he watches the warm, giggly middle baskets below with envy -> he climbs back down into the snug middle -> he learns the cozy crowded middle, not the lofty top, is where the good stuff is.

stories.title: Story 35: Scallion Pancake & the Great Flip-Off
stories.setting: A sizzling griddle-cart corner in Taichung
stories.theme: Showing off is more fun when you bring a friend along.
stories.premise: Cōng Cōng challenges the whole street to a pancake-flipping contest but keeps flipping himself into trouble, until anxious Pudding accidentally out-wobbles everyone and the two combine talents.

stories.title: Story 36: Oyster Omelet & the Tide-Pool Song
stories.setting: A seaside night market in Tainan by the tidal flats
stories.theme: Being soft is its own kind of strong.
stories.premise: Shy Wō Wō can barely speak above a whisper until the little oysters in her omelet go quiet from homesickness, and she finds her voice singing them a sea-lullaby that carries across the whole market.

stories.title: Stinky Tofu & the Lights-Out Hide-and-Seek
stories.mainCharacter: Chòu Chòu (Stinky Tofu) — the bold, pungent fried-tofu cube
stories.setting: A maze-like old shophouse alley during a power-out game of hide-and-seek
stories.theme: The very thing you'd hide can be what helps everyone find each other
stories.premise: During a lights-out game of hide-and-seek in the twisty alleys, the little snacks get hopelessly lost in the dark. Chòu Chòu, who usually tries to hide his powerful aroma, realizes his unmistakable smell is the one thing that can guide every lost player back to the group — and for once he proudly lets his scent lead the way home.
stories.arc: The snacks play hide-and-seek as the lights go out, and several get lost in the dark maze of alleys -> Chòu Chòu instinctively tries to tuck his smell away as always -> the lost players can't see a thing and start to worry -> he realizes his scent is a homing beacon and stops hiding it -> he leads everyone safely back, his 'flaw' the hero of the night.

stories.title: Story 38: Gua Bao & the Folded Hug
stories.setting: A lantern-lit alley diner in Keelung
stories.theme: There's always room to fold one more in.
stories.premise: On a rainy night, Guā Bāo keeps her diner warm by folding lost and lonely snacks into cozy hugs, until she runs out of room and the snacks learn to fold one another.

stories.title: Story 39: Popcorn Chicken & the Runaway Giggle
stories.setting: A neon Shilin Night Market snack stall
stories.theme: It's okay to slow down and count your crew.
stories.premise: The Kǎ Kǎ nuggets giggle so hard they scatter across the night market, and the smallest nugget must hop bravely from stall to stall to gather the whole bouncy crew back together before closing.

stories.title: Story 40: Braised Pork Rice & the Humble Bowl
stories.setting: A tiny family rice shop in old Tainan
stories.theme: Simple, done with love, outshines fancy.
stories.premise: When a glittery new dessert cart makes plain Lǔ Ròu feel boring, a hungry, tired traveler reminds him that a humble warm bowl is exactly the comfort the world needs at the end of a long day.

stories.title: Story 41: The Savory Squad & the Midnight Feast
stories.setting: A pop-up street-food alley that only appears at midnight
stories.theme: Sweet and savory are better together.
stories.premise: The new savory friends throw a midnight feast but argue with the dessert crowd over who rules the night market, until a hungry crowd proves a perfect night needs both sweet AND savory.

stories.title: Story 42: Tea Egg & the All-Night Store
stories.setting: A glowing 24-hour convenience store on a quiet rainy street
stories.theme: Small comforts keep the night feeling safe.
stories.premise: Wise little Dàn Dàn reads the cracks in his shell like fortunes to comfort late-night wanderers who stop by the all-night store, and helps a lost traveler find the way home.

stories.title: Story 43: Soy Milk & Youtiao & the Sunrise Dip
stories.setting: A steamy pre-dawn breakfast shop in Taipei
stories.theme: Best friends are better together — one dunk at a time.
stories.premise: Goofy Yóu Tiáo is terrified of his big morning dunk into warm soy milk until best pal Dòu Jiāng promises to catch him; together they wake the whole sleepy city with the smell of breakfast.

stories.title: Story 44: Radish Cake & the Breakfast Club
stories.setting: A neighborhood morning griddle stall
stories.theme: Crispy edges, soft heart — be both.
stories.premise: Dependable Luóbo Gāo organizes the breakfast crew for the morning rush, but a sleepy mix-up sends everyone to the wrong stalls; he must keep his cool (and crispy edges) to set the morning right.

stories.title: Story 45: Pepper Bun & the Clay-Oven Jump
stories.setting: A famous Raohe Night Market clay-oven stall
stories.theme: Courage is a leap, even when you're scared and warm.
stories.premise: Hú Jiāo is too scared to make the big jump off the blazing clay-oven wall when he's done baking, until popcorn chicken and friends form a soft, giggling landing pile below.

stories.title: Story 46: Chicken Cutlet & the Bigger-Than-Your-Face Show
stories.setting: A Fengjia Night Market main stage
stories.theme: Being big is great; being kind is greater.
stories.premise: Crowd-favorite Pái Pái loves being the biggest snack in the market until a tiny shy nugget gets stage fright; she gives up her spotlight to share the stage and discovers the warmest applause of all.

stories.title: Story 47: Tangyuan & the Thousand Sky Lanterns
stories.setting: Pingxi Sky Lantern Festival in the mountains
stories.theme: A wish shared lifts higher than a wish kept.
stories.premise: At the Pingxi festival, Tāng Yuán helps a nervous newcomer write and release their very first sky lantern, learning that the brightest wishes are the ones we send up for someone else.

stories.title: Story 48: Mooncake & the Mid-Autumn Moon
stories.setting: A rooftop family reunion under the full Mid-Autumn moon
stories.theme: Family is what makes any night feel full.
stories.premise: Elegant Yuè Bǐng hosts a rooftop reunion, but the moon hides behind clouds; he gathers everyone to glow together so warmly that the moon peeks out to join the party.

stories.title: Story 49: Zongzi & the Dragon-Boat Race
stories.setting: A Dragon Boat Festival river race in Lukang
stories.theme: Wrapped-up tight just means ready to ride.
stories.premise: Bundled-up Zòng Zi worries he's tied too tight to ever be fast, but in the splashy dragon-boat race he learns his snug wrapping is exactly what keeps his treasures safe through the wildest rapids.

stories.title: Story 50: The Grand Festival of Fifty Lights
stories.setting: A massive island-wide festival linking every night market by lantern-light
stories.theme: Halfway is worth a celebration when you've made it together.
stories.premise: To mark fifty stories of adventures, Boba rallies sweet and savory friends to light a chain of lanterns from north to south Taiwan, celebrating how far this growing family has come.
stories.guests: Niú Niú, Tāng Yuán, Egg Waffle

stories.title: Story 51: Aiyu & the Lantern Riddle Night
stories.setting: A temple courtyard riddle-lantern festival at night
stories.theme: Quiet cleverness shines just as bright.
stories.premise: Shy, translucent Aiyu is too timid to shout out answers at the lantern-riddle festival, but her honest, clever whispers solve the trickiest riddle of the night and light the grandest lantern.

stories.title: Turnip Cake & the Lucky-Word Banner
stories.mainCharacter: Cài Tóu Guǒ (Turnip/Radish Cake) — a humble, steamy, square savory cake, shy with words
stories.setting: A family kitchen and front doorway during Lunar New Year's Eve preparations
stories.theme: A wish written for your home is a wish for everyone in it
stories.premise: On New Year's Eve, shy Turnip Cake is asked to write the lucky red banner for the door but freezes, afraid his clumsy brushstrokes will jinx the whole year. He discovers the banner isn't about perfect calligraphy — it's about naming the hopes you hold for the people inside, and his wobbly, heartfelt characters become the warmest welcome on the street.
stories.arc: Turnip Cake is handed the brush for the all-important door banner and panics -> he practices and smudges and crumples sheet after sheet -> an elder reminds him a couplet is a wish, not a test -> he writes simple, honest words of warmth for his household -> neighbors stop to admire the heartfelt banner as the new year arrives.

stories.title: Story 53: The Earth God & the Lucky Corner
stories.setting: A tiny roadside Earth God temple beside the night market
stories.theme: Looking after your little corner helps the whole world.
stories.premise: The kindly tiny Earth God notices a forgotten corner of the market feeling lonely, and with lucky candies and gentle nudges he helps the snacks there find their place and their friends.

stories.title: Story 54: Moon Rabbit & the Mochi-Pounding Lullaby
stories.setting: The surface of the moon, glowing above sleeping Taiwan
stories.theme: Gentle rhythms carry everyone to sleep.
stories.premise: High on the moon, the dreamy Moon Rabbit pounds mochi to a lullaby beat, and when Mochi floats up on a moonbeam to help, the two send sweet sleepy dreams drifting down over the whole island.

stories.title: Story 55: The Little Tiger God Under the Table
stories.setting: Under the offering table of a cozy neighborhood temple
stories.theme: Even guardians need a friend and a nap.
stories.premise: The plump little clay Tiger God is lonely guarding the temple all by himself, until Braised Pork Rice shares his lunch and the two become the coziest guardian duo on the block.

stories.title: Story 56: Aiyu & the Friendly Mist Spirits
stories.setting: A misty mountain stream where aiyu seeds are rubbed
stories.theme: Kindness clears away even the foggiest worries.
stories.premise: Tiny, shy mist spirits keep getting lost in the mountain fog and bumping into things; honest Aiyu, who can see clearly through her translucent self, gently guides each one safely home.

stories.title: Story 57: Tea Leaf & the Cloud Sea of Alishan
stories.setting: The misty high peaks and sunrise cloud-sea of Alishan
stories.theme: Patience lets the best things unfurl.
stories.premise: Calm tea-leaf Ā-Lǐ teaches an impatient young leaf that rushing only makes you bitter; together they wait for the perfect sunrise over the cloud-sea and unfurl their fragrance to greet the day.

stories.title: Story 58: The Lucky Cat & the Incense-Curl Wishes
stories.setting: A warm Longshan-style temple at dusk, full of curling incense
stories.theme: Good wishes, like incense, rise gently and reach far.
stories.premise: A worried little snack comes to the temple with a wish too small to say out loud; the gentle Earth God and a friendly waving lucky-cat statue show that no kind wish is ever too small to matter.

stories.title: Story 59: Taro & the Southern Sugar Fields
stories.setting: Sugarcane fields and a vintage sugar-railway in Tainan
stories.theme: Good things take time to steam — and to grow.
stories.premise: Patient Taro begins an island road trip in the sunny south, riding the old sugar-train through cane fields and teaching a restless brown-sugar friend that the sweetest things ripen slowly.

stories.title: Story 60: Mango & the Mango Capital Race
stories.setting: The mango orchards and sunny roads of Yujing, Tainan
stories.theme: Home is the sweetest finish line.
stories.premise: Speedy Mango races through Taiwan's mango capital during peak harvest, but slows down to help a sun-wilted little mango find shade, learning that the best races leave no friend behind.

stories.title: Sweet Potato & the Lantern-Float River Night
stories.setting: A slow river at night during a floating water-lantern ceremony in eastern Taiwan
stories.theme: Letting go is sometimes braver than holding on
stories.premise: At the river's floating-lantern night, a little snack clutches a worry he can't bear to release onto the water. Street-smart Sweet Potato — who once buried himself deep in the earth and had to let the farmer dig him up — gently shares that letting a thing drift away can be the bravest move of all, and together they set the worry-lantern gently onto the current.
stories.arc: A small friend grips his worry-lantern, unable to set it on the river -> Sweet Potato notices and sits beside him on the bank -> Sweet Potato tells of being dug from the dark earth and learning to let go -> they count to three and release the lantern together -> they watch it join a river of golden lights drifting peacefully downstream.

stories.title: Story 62: Coconut Jelly & the Kenting Tide
stories.setting: The southern beaches and coral reefs of Kenting
stories.theme: Go with the flow, but reach for friends when the tide turns.
stories.premise: Chill surfer Coconut Jelly teaches the new savory crew to ride the gentle Kenting waves, but when a sudden tide sweeps a friend out, he learns even the most laid-back dude must paddle hard for the ones he loves.

stories.title: Story 63: Boba & the Train Around the Island
stories.setting: A round-the-island railway journey aboard a cozy night train
stories.theme: The journey is the best part — bounce through it.
stories.premise: Bouncy Boba sets off to ride the train all the way around Taiwan, collecting a snack friend at every station, until the whole carriage becomes a rolling, laughing party of new and old pals.
stories.guests: Pái Pái (Chicken Cutlet), Cōng Cōng (Scallion Pancake)

stories.title: Nougat & the Borrowed-Umbrella Chain
stories.mainCharacter: Niúgá Táng (Milk Nougat) — a chewy, milky-white candy studded with nuts, cheerful and a bit forgetful
stories.setting: A rainy shopping street with a long covered arcade in Jiufen
stories.theme: A small kindness passed on travels farther than one kept
stories.premise: Caught in a downpour, Nougat is lent an umbrella by a stranger who says only 'pass it on when you can.' Instead of keeping the cozy umbrella, Nougat starts a chain of lending it down the rainy street, and by nightfall a single borrowed umbrella has kept a dozen soggy snacks dry — proving a kindness shared keeps spreading long after you let it go.
stories.arc: Nougat is soaked and shivering until a stranger lends an umbrella with one rule: pass it on -> he's tempted to keep it dry and warm -> he spots someone wetter than him and hands it over -> the umbrella travels snack to snack down the arcade -> by night it has sheltered the whole street, and the kindness loops back to Nougat himself.

stories.title: Story 65: Douhua & the Beitou Hot Spring
stories.setting: A steamy Beitou hot-spring bathhouse in the hills
stories.theme: Be soft, be still, let your worries melt.
stories.premise: Gentle Douhua leads a tired group of friends to soak in the warm Beitou hot springs, where she teaches a frazzled, overheated Pepper Bun the quiet art of letting tension melt away in the steam.

stories.title: Story 66: Red Bean & the First Warm Day of Spring
stories.setting: A countryside cherry-blossom hillside in Wuling as winter ends
stories.theme: After every cold spell, warmth comes cooking back.
stories.premise: As the last frost lifts, nurturing Red Bean cooks a warm welcome-spring soup under the cherry blossoms, coaxing sleepy hibernating snacks to wake up gently to the new season.

stories.title: Story 67: Shaved Ice & the Plum Rain Season
stories.setting: A drippy night market during Taiwan's plum-rain season
stories.theme: Even drama queens shine brightest helping others.
stories.premise: During the endless plum-rains, dramatic Shaved Ice melts with worry that nobody wants cold treats in soggy weather, until she learns to throw the coziest rainy-day party the market has ever seen.

stories.title: Story 68: Mango & the Cozy Typhoon Day
stories.setting: A snug apartment with friends as a gentle typhoon passes outside
stories.theme: Sometimes the best race is the one to the snack cupboard.
stories.premise: Speedy Mango is grumpy that a typhoon cancels his big race, until friends turn the rainy indoor day into the most fun pillow-fort, board-game, and snack adventure of the whole summer.

stories.title: Candied Tomato & the Is-It-Fruit-or-Candy Riddle
stories.mainCharacter: Mì Fānqié (Candied Tomato) — cherry tomatoes on a stick in a glossy crackly sugar shell dusted with sour plum powder, giggly and tangy-sweet
stories.setting: A buzzing Tainan night-market 'guess the snack' game stall
stories.theme: Joy doesn't care what category you fit in
stories.premise: When a night-market game declares snacks must be either 'fruit' or 'candy,' poor Candied Tomato doesn't fit either box and feels left out — until she proves that the most delightful treats are the ones that are happily, deliciously both.

stories.title: Pearl Barley & the Counting-Stars Sleepover
stories.mainCharacter: Yìrén (Pearl Barley / Job's Tears) — small, pale, pearly grains who travel as a chattery cluster
stories.setting: A rooftop sleepover under the autumn sky in a quiet riverside town
stories.theme: You don't have to fill every silence — some quiet is for wondering
stories.premise: The Pearl Barley grains never stop chattering, and at the rooftop sleepover their nonstop talking keeps everyone awake. One grain learns that when you finally hush and look up, the quiet between words is where the biggest, most wonderful thoughts have room to grow — and counting stars together in silence is its own kind of conversation.
stories.arc: The Pearl Barley cluster talks over everyone at the sleepover, nobody can sleep -> their endless chatter even drowns out a shy friend's wish to share something -> a gentle nudge to just look up at the sky -> they fall quiet and discover the awe of the silent star-filled night -> they learn that companionable quiet can say more than chatter.

stories.title: Hot Pot Mochi & the Frozen-Lake Skating Wobble
stories.mainCharacter: Shāo Má Shǔ (Toasted Mochi) — a puffy grilled mochi dusted in soybean powder, eager but unsteady
stories.setting: A rare frozen alpine lake high in the mountains on a crisp winter day
stories.theme: Falling down is just part of learning something new
stories.premise: On the rare day the high mountain lake freezes, Toasted Mochi wants to ice-skate gracefully on his very first try and is crushed every time he flops onto his squishy bottom. With friends cheering each tumble, he learns that every fall is a step toward gliding — and by sunset his wobbly, giggly skating has turned into the happiest, most fearless slide on the whole lake.
stories.arc: Toasted Mochi straps on skates expecting instant grace and immediately flops -> embarrassed by fall after fall, he wants to quit -> friends cheer his tumbles instead of laughing at them -> he keeps trying, falling, and getting up, improving bit by bit -> by dusk he glides freely, proud that every fall taught him to skate.

stories.title: Story 72: Egg Waffle & the Ring-Toss Champion
stories.setting: The classic carnival game-stall row of a night market
stories.theme: Winning is fun; cheering others on is funner.
stories.premise: Showman Egg Waffle is determined to win every night-market game stall in one night, but learns the real prize is helping a nervous newcomer finally win their very first goldfish-scoop.

stories.title: Almond Tofu & the Cloud-Sorting Job
stories.mainCharacter: Xìngrén Dòufu (Almond Tofu) — a soft, pale, jiggly almond pudding who is a worrier about order and neatness
stories.setting: A misty mountain teahouse perched in the clouds above Maokong
stories.theme: Not everything needs to be tidy to be lovely
stories.premise: Fussy Almond Tofu is hired to sort the teahouse's drifting clouds into neat fluffy rows for the view, but the clouds keep blending and swirling no matter how hard he tidies. He learns that the messiest, mingled cloud-sea is the most beautiful sight of all, and that some lovely things can't — and shouldn't — be kept in tidy lines.
stories.arc: Almond Tofu accepts the impossible job of arranging the clouds -> he frets and herds them into rows that instantly drift apart -> mounting frustration and very silly cloud-wrangling mishaps -> a wise old teapot shows him the wild, swirling cloud-sea at sunset -> he lets go of tidiness and finally just enjoys the gloriously messy view.

stories.title: Tempura Fishcake & the Hot-Spring Egg Race
stories.mainCharacter: Tián Bù Lǎ (Taiwanese Tianbula / fishcake) — a chewy, ridged, golden fried fishcake who is patient and methodical
stories.setting: A volcanic hot-spring village in Beitou where eggs cook in the steaming pools
stories.theme: Doing one careful thing well beats doing ten things in a hurry
stories.premise: When a crowd of snacks rushes to soft-boil their eggs in the famous hot springs all at once, they snatch them out too early and end up with a runny mess. Methodical Tianbula shows them that the trick isn't speed — it's lowering one egg gently, timing it just right, and waiting patiently for the perfect, jiggly result everyone's been hurrying past.
stories.arc: Everyone races to dunk eggs in the steaming pools to be first to eat -> they yank them out too soon and grumble at the gloppy results -> impatient retries make a bigger mess -> Tianbula calmly demonstrates careful timing with a single egg -> the crowd slows down, copies him, and shares a basket of perfect spring-cooked eggs.

stories.title: Story 75: Passion Fruit & the Sour-Dare Derby
stories.setting: A carnival dare-booth corner of a lively night market
stories.theme: The boldest dare is being kind when no one dares you to.
stories.premise: Prankster Passion Fruit runs a sour-face dare derby, daring everyone to the most pucker-worthy challenges, until shy Stinky Tofu out-dares them all by bravely being himself — the boldest dare of all.

stories.title: Story 76: Boba & the Great Bubble-Tea Shake-Off
stories.setting: A buzzing bubble-tea shop championship in Taichung (boba's birthplace)
stories.theme: You don't have to be on top to be the heart of the drink.
stories.premise: In Taichung, the home of bubble tea, Boba competes in a shake-off to be the star pearl, but learns that the best cup is the one where brown sugar, tea, and pearls all dance together.

stories.title: Salty Crisp Chicken & the Spice-Drawer Mystery
stories.mainCharacter: Yán Sū Jī (Salt-and-Pepper Crispy Chicken) — a crunchy, basil-flecked fried snack with a detective's magnifying glass
stories.setting: A bustling Shilin night-market fry stall after closing, lit by a single bulb
stories.theme: Curiosity solves more than strength ever could
stories.premise: When the stall's beloved spice drawer goes missing right before the morning rush, self-styled detective Salty Crisp Chicken cracks the case not by being the biggest or boldest but by asking 'why' and 'why' and 'why' again, following a trail of fragrant basil leaves to a sleepy mouse who only wanted to smell something nice.
stories.arc: The whole stall panics — no spices means no flavor for tomorrow -> Salty Crisp Chicken refuses to just shove things around and instead investigates clues -> wrong guesses and silly red herrings (a sneeze, a runaway peppercorn) -> the basil trail leads to a tiny mouse nest -> gentle questioning solves it, the spices come home, and curiosity wins the day.

stories.title: Story 78: Willa Wobble & the Night-Market Pinball Quest
stories.setting: A retro pinball-and-pachinko arcade tucked in a night market
stories.theme: The smallest player can rack up the biggest heart-points.
stories.premise: Crossover guest Willa Wobble, tiniest of penguins, visits the night market and proves that being small is an advantage in the bounciest pinball quest, with Boba bouncing along as her lucky ball.

stories.title: Story 79: Egg Waffle & the Big Talent Show
stories.setting: A community-stage talent show in a covered market plaza
stories.theme: Everyone's got a talent worth cheering.
stories.premise: Egg Waffle organizes a market talent show and panics when no one signs up; he learns to coax out everyone's hidden talents — even Tea Egg's quiet fortune-reading — for the warmest show ever.

stories.title: Bubble Waffle Sisters & the Kite Festival Sky
stories.mainCharacter: Shuāng Bāo Tāi (the Double-Bun Twins) — two fried twin-dough buns joined at the middle, one daring and one cautious
stories.setting: The windy grassy hills of a Hsinchu kite festival on a blustery afternoon
stories.theme: Two who pull in different directions can still fly the same kite
stories.premise: The Double-Bun Twins want to launch the grandest kite at the festival, but one twin yanks the string tight while the other lets it loose, and their kite keeps nose-diving. They learn that flying isn't about one of them winning the tug — it's about feeling the wind together and pulling at the same gentle moment.
stories.arc: The joined twins each grab an end of the kite string and argue over technique -> crash after embarrassing crash on the hill -> they stop competing and start listening to the wind -> they discover that taking turns easing and tugging makes the kite soar -> their kite climbs highest of all, lifted by their teamwork, not their tugging.

stories.title: Lychee & the Hand-Me-Down Fan
stories.setting: A grandmother fruit-seller's shaded stall at a sweltering traditional market
stories.theme: The oldest, plainest things often hold the most love
stories.premise: Fancy Lychee is mortified that her elegant new silk fan tears on the hottest day, and turns up her nose at the worn, faded paper fan an old fruit-seller offers her. But the shabby little fan turns out to have been hand-painted with love and to cool better than any fancy one — teaching Lychee that worth and beauty hide in well-loved old things, not just new finery.
stories.arc: Lychee shows off her dazzling new silk fan at the market -> the delicate fan rips in the heat and she's left fanning frantically -> a kindly old seller offers a battered, faded paper fan -> Lychee reluctantly accepts, then discovers it's lovingly hand-painted and cools beautifully -> she treasures the humble heirloom and thanks the seller warmly.

stories.title: Iron Egg & the Lost-and-Found Lighthouse
stories.mainCharacter: Tiě Dàn (Iron Egg) — a tiny, dark, chewy salt-and-soy braised egg from Tamsui, gruff and crusty on the outside
stories.setting: The old Tamsui (Danshui) harbor and its red-brick lighthouse at dusk
stories.theme: What looks tough on the outside can be the gentlest helper of all
stories.premise: Crusty little Iron Egg is sure his hard, wrinkled shell means he's no good for soft jobs, until the harbor lighthouse keeper falls ill and a fog rolls in. Iron Egg discovers his dark, dense little body is the perfect weight to keep the signal-lantern's pulley steady, and his gruff foghorn voice gently calls every lost fishing-snack safely back to the docks.
stories.arc: Iron Egg grumbles that nobody wants a tough, ugly snack -> fog swallows the harbor and a boat of little snacks can't find shore -> the lighthouse lamp keeps slipping -> Iron Egg anchors the pulley with his weight and booms a soft, steady call across the water -> every boat finds home, and the toughest snack turns out to be the warmest beacon.

stories.title: Brown Sugar & the Happy Little Mistake
stories.mainCharacter: Hēi Táng (Brown Sugar) — a warm dark-amber sugar cube with a cozy molasses glow, kindly and a little clumsy
stories.setting: A bubbling boba-syrup kitchen at dusk
stories.theme: A little imperfection can make you richer, not ruined
stories.premise: Brown Sugar is mortified when he bubbles a moment too long and turns a deeper, darker, slightly-burnt shade — until everyone tastes the new caramel-deep flavor and discovers his 'mistake' is the most delicious syrup the tea shop has ever poured.

stories.title: Story 84: Peanut Ice Roll & the Weird-Delicious Stand
stories.setting: A quirky experimental food stand at a creative night market
stories.theme: Trust the weird — surprising can be wonderful.
stories.premise: Cool maverick Bǐng Bǐng (peanut candy, ice cream, and cilantro in a wrap) opens a 'weird-delicious' stand that everyone doubts, until his surprising combo wins over the most stubborn skeptic in the market.

stories.title: Cuttlefish Ball & the Tangled Lantern Strings
stories.mainCharacter: Huāzhī Wán (Cuttlefish Ball) — a bouncy, springy seafood ball on a skewer, eager and a little frazzled
stories.setting: A temple courtyard the morning the festival lanterns must be hung
stories.theme: Asking for help untangles what you can't sort out alone
stories.premise: Determined to hang all the festival lanterns himself, springy Cuttlefish Ball bounces around tying strings until he's hopelessly tangled in a giant knot of lantern cords. Too proud to call out at first, he finally squeaks for help — and learns that the knot loosens in minutes when many hands each take one string, while one frazzled snack could never undo it alone.
stories.arc: Cuttlefish Ball insists on hanging every lantern by himself before the festival -> he bounces and ties until he's bound up in a snarl of strings -> he struggles silently, embarrassed to ask -> he finally calls 'bāngmáng!' and friends each grab a strand -> the knot falls away, lanterns rise, and he learns help shared lightens any tangle.

stories.title: Sago Pudding & the Sandcastle That Wouldn't Stay
stories.mainCharacter: Xī Mǐ Lù (Sago Pudding) — a cool, milky pudding full of tiny translucent sago pearls, gentle and accepting
stories.setting: A breezy white-sand beach on Penghu island at low tide
stories.theme: It's okay when something beautiful doesn't last
stories.premise: Sago Pudding helps a heartbroken little friend build the grandest sandcastle on the beach, only for the tide to wash it away. Instead of sadness, gentle Sago Pudding shows that the fun was in the building, the castle lives on in their memory, and tomorrow's beach is a fresh blank canvas — teaching that some lovely things are meant to be temporary and that's exactly what makes them special.
stories.arc: Sago Pudding and a friend build an elaborate sandcastle together -> the tide creeps in and the friend panics to save it -> the waves wash the castle flat -> the friend is crushed, but Sago Pudding reframes the joy of building and remembering -> they laugh, scoop fresh sand, and plan tomorrow's castle, at peace with impermanence.

stories.title: Wintermelon Tea & the Sound-Collector's Jar
stories.mainCharacter: Dōngguā Chá (Wintermelon Tea) — a tall, amber, sweet-and-cooling drink in a glass bottle, an absent-minded collector
stories.setting: A cluttered old apothecary-and-bottle shop in Tainan's lantern-lit back lanes
stories.theme: Listening closely is a kind of giving
stories.premise: Chatty Wintermelon Tea loves collecting interesting sounds in empty glass jars, but when a lonely new snack arrives who is too sad to speak, his jars stay empty. He learns to stop talking and simply listen — and discovers that letting someone be heard is the most generous gift of all, filling his quietest jar with the truest sound.
stories.arc: Wintermelon Tea proudly shows off his jars of bottled sounds -> a hushed, homesick newcomer won't say a word, so the collector has nothing to catch -> he keeps chattering and filling the silence himself, missing the point -> he finally goes quiet and listens with his whole glassy self -> the newcomer opens up, and that gentle telling becomes the most precious sound he's ever kept.

stories.title: Peanut Brittle & the Stuck-Together Day
stories.mainCharacter: Huāshēng Táng (Peanut Brittle) — a crunchy, golden, glued-together slab of candied peanuts, loud and busy
stories.setting: A sunny candy-maker's workshop on a humid summer afternoon
stories.theme: Slowing down lets you notice who's right beside you
stories.premise: Busy, always-rushing Peanut Brittle prides himself on getting everything done fast, until a sticky-humid day makes the whole workshop go gooey and slow. Forced to wait for the candy to set, he finally sits still long enough to really talk to the quiet little peanut who has been stuck beside him the whole time — and finds his oldest friend was right there all along.
stories.arc: Peanut Brittle zooms through chores, brushing past everyone -> the humid day softens the candy so nothing can be hurried -> he fidgets, impatient, with nothing to do but wait -> stuck beside a shy peanut he'd never really noticed, he finally chats and listens -> he learns slowing down let him find a friend he'd been rushing right past.

stories.title: Sun Cake & the Trail of Golden Crumbs
stories.mainCharacter: Tàiyáng Bǐng (Sun Cake) — a flaky golden Taichung pastry shaped like a little sun, sheds crumbs everywhere, sunny and shy
stories.setting: The winding lanes of old Taichung at golden hour
stories.theme: The little bits you scatter can lead friends right to you
stories.premise: Flaky Sun Cake is embarrassed that she leaves a trail of crumbs everywhere she goes — until a lost, lonely little friend follows that exact golden trail straight to her and a warm circle of new friends.

stories.title: Story 90: The Great Night-Market Blackout
stories.setting: A whole night market plunged into a sudden, gentle power outage
stories.theme: When the lights go out, friends become the light.
stories.premise: When the night market's lights blink out, cool-headed Grass Jelly keeps everyone calm while glowing snacks (Aiyu, Starfruit, Mooncake) light the way and a candlelit feast turns the dark into the coziest night ever.

stories.title: Story 91: The Hundred-Snack Cooking School
stories.setting: A bustling pop-up cooking school teaching young snacks the old recipes
stories.theme: Pass it on — that's how flavor lasts forever.
stories.premise: Humble Lǔ Ròu and the savory elders open a cooking school to teach a new batch of tiny snacks the cherished old recipes, learning that teaching is its own delicious reward.
stories.guests: Niú Niú, Red Bean, Cōng Cōng

stories.title: Story 92: Boba & the Letter to Every Friend
stories.setting: A late-night writing desk lit by a paper lantern, all across the island by post
stories.theme: Reaching out keeps a family close.
stories.premise: Boba decides to invite every friend — sweet and savory, near and far — to a great gathering, and bounces all over Taiwan delivering hand-written letters, gathering stories along the way.

stories.title: Story 93: The Earth God & the Island-Wide Blessing
stories.setting: Earth God temples across Taiwan, linked on a single festival night
stories.theme: A blessing shared corner-to-corner covers the whole island.
stories.premise: The kindly Earth Gods of every little corner join hands one festival night to bless the whole island and its snacks, lighting a gentle golden warmth from mountains to sea ahead of the big reunion.
stories.guests: Yù Tù (Moon Rabbit), Xiǎo Hǔ Yé (Tiger God)

stories.title: Story 94: Tea Egg & the Map of Cracks
stories.setting: A quiet hilltop overlooking all the night-market lights of the island
stories.theme: Every little path leads home if you follow it kindly.
stories.premise: Wise Tea Egg realizes the crackle-lines on his shell form a map of every friend's journey, and he uses it to guide all the scattered snacks toward the gathering place for the grand reunion.

stories.title: Story 95: The Sweet-and-Savory Cook-Off Truce
stories.setting: A grand pre-reunion cook-off in a giant covered market hall
stories.theme: The best meal has a little of everything.
stories.premise: A friendly cook-off between the Savory Squad and the dessert crew threatens to split the family in two right before the reunion, until they discover the winning dish is one they make together.
stories.guests: Shaved Ice, Tāng Yuán, Pái Pái

stories.title: Lantern Squid & the Tide-Chart Crossing
stories.mainCharacter: Yóu Yú Gēng (Squid Thick-Soup) — a savory, peppery squid soup in a bowl, a practical seafarer type
stories.setting: The fishing harbor of an offshore island, planning the boat trip to the mainland reunion
stories.theme: Knowing the right moment to go is its own kind of wisdom
stories.premise: The far-flung island snacks are desperate to set off for the grand reunion right away, but the boat can only cross safely at high tide. Practical Squid Soup reads the old tide-chart and convinces the eager crowd to wait for the perfect moment — and when the tide finally lifts the boat, their patience carries them across smoothly, arriving in time and all in one happy piece.
stories.arc: The island snacks pack up, frantic to leave immediately for the reunion -> Squid Soup warns the harbor is too shallow until high tide -> the impatient crowd grumbles and nearly launches anyway -> they wait, watching the water rise on the tide-chart -> at high tide the boat glides out easily, and they reach the mainland reunion safe and joyful.

stories.title: Story 97: Shaved Ice & the Grandest Decorations
stories.setting: A vast festival hall being decorated for the hundredth-story reunion
stories.theme: More is more — but the most is everyone pitching in.
stories.premise: Dramatic Shaved Ice takes charge of decorating the grand reunion hall and goes gloriously overboard, until friends help her see that the warmest decoration is the crowd of friends themselves.

stories.title: Story 98: The Night Before the Reunion
stories.setting: A hushed, cozy guesthouse the night before the grand gathering
stories.theme: Calm before the joy is a gift too.
stories.premise: On the quiet night before the hundredth-story reunion, gentle Douhua moves through the guesthouse soothing excited, sleepless friends, helping the whole family rest up for the biggest day yet.

stories.title: Story 99: Sunrise Over the Whole Island
stories.setting: Dawn breaking over all of Taiwan as everyone travels to the reunion
stories.theme: A new day, gently begun, holds everything.
stories.premise: Dawn-gentle Soy Milk and Youtiao wake the whole island with a warm breakfast as every snack — sweet and savory, old and new — sets out on the morning roads toward the grand hundredth reunion.

stories.title: Story 100: The Grand Island Reunion
stories.setting: A spectacular island-wide festival uniting every night market in Taiwan
stories.theme: A hundred stories, one big delicious family.
stories.premise: At last, every friend from all one hundred stories — sweet and savory, fruit and folklore, new and old — gathers for the grandest reunion feast Taiwan has ever seen, celebrating the family they've become.
stories.guests: The entire cast: desserts, savory squad, folklore friends, and penguin/Piggle-Wiggle crossover guests
